speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what is the total number of business closures and formations since the start of the circuit breaker period; (b) what is the sectoral breakdown of those most affected to the least affected; (c) what is the Ministry's outlook on the business cessation trend and sectoral implications for the remainder of 2020 even as the global and domestic economies gradually open up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Most sectors saw a fall in the formation of new business entities during this period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Outward-oriented sectors such as wholesale trade will be adversely affected by the global economic slowdown, while the air transport and tourism sectors will continue to be badly affected by travel restrictions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Sectors such as retail and food services will also be adversely impacted by reduced demand from tourists and local consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: On the other hand, there are sectors which continue to grow, such as biomedical manufacturing and the information and communications sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These happened even before COVID-19, but with COVID-19, we must expect the situation to worsen and these numbers to go up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Senior Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam is chairing the National Jobs Council.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This includes initiatives to expand job opportunities in both the public and private sectors, provide a range of traineeships for jobseekers to gain industry-relevant experience and build professional networks, as well as increase training capacity to enable jobseekers to upgrade their skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: There is no certainty that we will succeed in creating all the jobs and opportunities in adifficult economic environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We will bring on board all tripartite partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We will support one another and spare no effort to achieve our goals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: And we will overcome this crisis as one united Team Singapore.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In relation to his answer, with MTI and EDB's announcement that from January to April, there is an investment commitment of about $13 billion coming to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In terms of job creation, going forward, and also those investment commitments beyond April to end of 2020 and possibly early first half of 2021, can Senior Minister of State share a bit more about whether the trajectory of investment commitments will continue to be positive and in which sectors in particular, going forward?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We are heartened that investors continue to have confidence in Singapore and that is very important because we do need to create jobs from a range of different sources – public sector, but also private sector.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As to how well we can continue to attract investments, I think a key factor is how well we respond to this crisis as a country.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If we can demonstrate resilience, fortitude, we can show unity, we are able to overcome this crisis together as one united Team Singapore, we are able to rally our tripartite partners to work closely together, I think we can inspire confidence and we can attract investments.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We can demonstrate that Singapore has the capabilities and the resilience to overcome this crisis.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is very important – how we respond to this crisis together.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We continue to have to remain as an attractive business hub because it is not just about retaining our current capabilities and companies but also attracting new ones.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I shared earlier in my main reply that there will be some sectors that will show a decline and some sectors will show growth.
